title: Book Two · Chapter 39: One at a Time
story:
Miss Wu brings the reading folder to the front on Thursday.

Ronan sits up. Leo stops rolling his pencil.

“I read your answers,” she says. “On Monday, we will look at them together. One person at a time.”

“Today?” Ronan asks.

“Monday. I will have a little time for each of you.”

“Will we read them aloud?”

“To me. Not to the whole class.”

Ronan looks at the folder. The folder is thin. But Ronan cannot see his answers through the cover.

Miss Wu writes a new question on the board. It is about numbers. The class opens its books.

At break, Jun comes to the window desk.

“Did you get the gate question?”

“I put an answer.”

“So did I.”

Ronan wants to ask Jun about the person at the gate. But Leo is standing beside them. Ronan takes a scrap from his bag instead.

“Can you make a square with one fold?” he asks.

Jun looks at the paper. One side is longer than the other.

“Not with that shape.”

“You can fold the corner,” Leo says.

They try it. One small strip still sticks out. Jun folds it behind the square.

“Now it has a tail.”

“A square kite,” Ronan says.

He puts the paper above his head. Leo blows at it. The tail touches Ronan's nose, and he lowers it again.

After school, Dad meets him near the main road. Dad has finished early today. He carries a little bag of screws from the shop.

Ronan asks about the old wooden box.

“I am making room for the drawer,” Dad says.

“More wood?”

“Less in one place. Not too much. I need it to slide, not fall out.”

They stop at the edge of the road. A cart comes past, then another. Dad waits until the way is clear.

“What if it sticks again?” Ronan asks.

“Then I must look again.”

“Will she be angry?”

“She may be. She waited before.”

Ronan looks at the bag in Dad's hand. One screw is smaller than all the rest.

“Do you like fixing it?”

“Some of the work. I do not like the mistake.”

At home, Mum wants to hear about his early finish. Dad sits beside her. They talk about Mr Sun's next jobs while Ronan puts his school things away.

He sets the date paper flat. Tuesday's task is already over. He draws a little line below it and writes Monday.

There are several days before the talk with Miss Wu.

Ronan opens his own book. He reads a page, then looks at the small paper square on the bed.

He takes it to the window. A little wind lifts its tail. He puts it down before it blows into Mum's thread.

Then he goes back to his book.
